To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the carbonation efficiency of metal wastes is affected by S/L ratio and that the structure of the precipitated calcium carbonate is different from that obtained by carbonation of natural minerals.
the carbonation efficiency of metal slags increases when the S/L is decreased, because of the diluting effect.

(i) the carbonation efficiency of the multi-step mineralization processes employing waste materials is affected by the S/L ratio; (ii) GGBS and PS are more efficient than SS in the carbonation reaction; (iii) the structure of carbonated products is affected by the type of waste employed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a process to treat metal wastes and produce carbonated materials, which can be employed for the storage of CO2.
the development of an innovative technology to store CO2, using waste materials, and with the characterization of the carbonation process.
the development of an innovative and sustainable process for carbon capture and storage (CCS), based on mineral carbonation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mineral carbonation of metal waste streams is an attractive technology for CO2 storage and the process can be easily optimized by varying the S/L ratio.

, for the three materials investigated in this work, the carbonation efficiencies increased with decreasing S/L ratios, and the carbonated residues are mainly composed by calcium carbonate, which is a stable and insoluble phase.
the S/L ratio is a key factor in the efficiency of the mineral carbonation of waste materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carbonation of metal slags can be considered as a viable technology to reduce CO2 emissions.
carbonation of waste materials is a promising technology for CO2 storage and that it can be optimized through the control of process variables.
carbonated products obtained from waste streams can be considered as a potential material to be used in building applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given material, the S/L ratio can affect the carbonation efficiency.
, for the materials investigated in this paper, the efficiency of the carbonation process increases when the S/L decreases, but the energy required to mix the solid and liquid phases also increases.
the carbonation process is highly dependent on the solid to liquid ratio.
